'''Mario Hezonja''' ({{IPA|hr|ˌmâːrio ˈxêzoɲa|hr}}; born 25 February 1995) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed '''Super Mario,''' he has represents the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]] in international competition. He was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]].

==Junior career==
Hezonja was promoted to the club level in his native Croatia when he was 12 years old, and at the age of 13, he stayed for two seasons with [[KK Dubrovnik|Dubrovnik]]. In 2010, Hezonja signed a contract with Croatian club [[KK Zagreb|Zagreb]]. In 2011, he won the [[Nike International Junior Tournament]] with Zagreb. He was also named to the All-Tournament team, alongside teammate [[Dario Šarić]]. He was forced to sit out the 2011–12 season because of [[Infectious mononucleosis|mononucleosis]].{{fact|date=March 2022}}

==Professional career==
===Barcelona (2012–2015)===
In July 2012, Hezonja signed a three-year contract with Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]], at the age of 17.<ref>{{cite web|last=Vera|first=Sergio|date=11 July 2012|title=Hezonja, la gran perla que aterriza en Barcelona|trans-title=Hezonja, the great pearl, lands in Barcelona|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/acb/hezonja-gran-perla-que-aterriza-barcelona-2058742|access-date=11 July 2012|publisher=Sport.es|language=es}}</ref> He also had an option to extend his contract for an additional four years with the club. His former club, Zagreb, also got €150,000 in the name of a buyout, as he was still under contract. For the 2012–13 season, he was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] to the [[reserve team]] of the club, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B|Barcelona B]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]], the [[Spanish basketball league system|Spanish second-tier level division]]. In 2012, Hezonja was nominated for the [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Young Player of the Year Award]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_MUMtgYLNGw6ts8a4RCdLp3.articleMode_on.html|title=Valanciunas Young Men's POY 2012|publisher=FIBA Europe.com|date=6 February 2013|access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> but [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] eventually won the award.{{fact|date=March 2022}}

[[File:Mario Hezonja1 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hezonja playing for FC Barcelona Under-18 at the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|EuroLeague Junior Tournament]] Finals in London, in May 2013]]
Hezonja played in the [[EuroLeague]] for the first time, in the [[2012–13 Euroleague|2012–13 season]]. He appeared in only 2 games, averaging 2.5 points and 2 rebounds per game.{{fact|date=March 2022}}

During the EuroLeague's [[2013–14 Euroleague|2013–14 season]], Hezonja played very limited minutes.{{fact|date=March 2022}}

Starting with the 2014–15 season, Hezonja's role in the team increased, from playing only during the [[garbage time]] in the previous season, to around 15 minutes per game.{{fact|date=March 2022}} On 1 February 2015, Hezonja hit 8-of-8 from the three-point line in a [[2014–15 ACB season|2014–15 Spanish League season]] game, in a 101–53 Barcelona win, against [[Bàsquet Manresa|La Bruixa d'Or Manresa]], becoming the [[2014–15 ACB season#Player of the week|Spanish League MVP for week 19 of the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=110483|title=Mario Hezonja, jugador de la jornada 19|language=es|publisher=ACB.com|date=1 February 2015|access-date=1 February 2015|archive-date=14 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214014633/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=110483|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barcelona finished their participation in the [[2014–15 Euroleague|2014–15 EuroLeague season]], after a quarterfinal series loss to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. Over 22 EuroLeague games played, Hezonja averaged 7.7 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist per game.{{fact|date=March 2022}}

On 23 April 2015, Hezonja declared himself eligible for the [[2015 NBA draft]], as an international "early-entrant", just days after Barcelona's elimination in the EuroLeague.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vecenie|first1=Sam|title=Croatian wing Mario Hezonja to declare for 2015 NBA Draft|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25161381/croatian-wing-mario-hezonja-to-declare-for-2015-nba-draft|access-date=24 April 2015|work=cbssports.com}}</ref> He had been identified as a potential lottery pick early in his career, and surprised some by opting not to declare for the draft in 2014, his first year of eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Mario-Hezonja-6392/|title=DraftExpress - Mario Hezonja DraftExpress Profile: Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook|access-date=10 May 2013|archive-date=25 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425230918/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Mario-Hezonja-6392/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Some Spanish and Croatian media saw this move as the player's response to poor communication throughout the final few months with Barcelona's head coach [[Xavier Pascual Vives|Xavi Pascual]]; Pascal denied any problems in communication.<ref>{{cite news|title=Súper Mario se harta y se apunta al Draft|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/04/24/baloncesto/acb/1429894073.html|access-date=24 April 2015|work=marca.com|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Ramos|first1=Jesús P.|title=Pascual: "Con Hezonja no pasa nada"|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/euroliga/20150401/102730430251/pascual-con-hezonja-no-pasa-nada.html|access-date=24 April 2015|work=mundodeportivo.com|date=1 April 2015|language=es}}</ref> Barcelona eventually finished the season losing in the [[2015 ACB Finals|final series]] of the [[2015 ACB Playoffs|2015 Spanish League playoffs]], after a 3–0 series loss to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid make it 4 out of 4|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/06/24/en/football/real_madrid/1435176357.html|access-date=24 June 2015|work=marca.com|date=24 June 2015|language=es}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2015–2018)===
On 25 June 2015, Hezonja was selected with the fifth overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cohen |first1=Josh |date=25 June 2015 |title=Magic Select Mario Hezonja with Fifth Overall Pick |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-select-mario-hezonja-fifth-overall-pick |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> On 10 July 2015, he signed a rookie scale contract with the Magic.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=10 July 2015 |title=Magic Sign Mario Hezonja |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-mario-hezonja |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref>

;2015–16 season
He made his debut for the Magic in the team's season-opening loss to the [[Washington Wizards]] on 28 October 2015, recording 11 points in 25 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite news |date=28 October 2015 |title=Late basket from Wall rallies Wizards over Magic 88-87 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story?id=13997053 |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> On 31 January 2016, he scored a then-season-high 17 points in a 119–114 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=31 January 2016 |title=Postgame Report: Magic vs. Celtics (1/31/16) |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/postgame-report-magic-vs.-celtics-1/31/16 |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> On 28 February 2016, he made his first career NBA start and dunked four seconds into the game, finishing with 13 points on 5-of-9 shooting in 27 minutes of action in a 130–116 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite news |date=28 February 2016 |title=Big Magic start dooms 76ers to eighth straight loss, 130-116 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap/_/gameId/400828768 |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> On 2 March 2016, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 102–89 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news |date=2 March 2016 |title=Vucevic scores 24 as Magic overwhelm Bulls, 102-89 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story?id=14889304 |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> On 11 April 2016, he set career highs with seven assists and five steals while scoring 19 points in a 107–98 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Blanco |first=Juan Carlos |date=11 April 2016 |title=Magic best Bucks, 107-98 |work=NBA.com |url=http://global.nba.com/news/magic-best-bucks-107-98/ |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref>

The Magic finished the season with 35–47 record, missing the [[2016 NBA playoffs|playoffs]]. Hezonja finished the season making 79 appearances with the averages of 6.1 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists on 43.3 field goal percentage.<ref>{{cite news |last=Savage |first=Dan |date=20 May 2016 |title=Magic Name Frank Vogel Head Coach |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-name-frank-vogel-head-coach |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref>

;2016–17 season
Under new head coach [[Frank Vogel]], Hezonja saw minutes reduction, mainly due to his mediocre defense.<ref name="2017evaluation">{{cite news|last1=Rossman-Reich|first1=Philip|title=2016-17 Orlando Magic Player Evaluations |url=https://orlandomagicdaily.com/2017/05/09/2016-17-orlando-magic-player-evaluations-mario-hezonja/|access-date=18 December 2017|work=orlandomagicdaily.com}}</ref> On 28 October 2016, Hezonja scored 13 points in a 108–82 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He tied that season high on 4 April 2017, registering another 13-point effort in a 122–102 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hezonma01/gamelog/2017/|title= 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=13 April 2017}}</ref> In the Magic's season finale on 12 April 2017, Hezonja grabbed a career-high 11 rebounds in a 113–109 win over Detroit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900595|title=Orlando hangs on to defeat Detroit 113-109|work=ESPN.com|date=12 April 2017|access-date=13 April 2017}}</ref>

Although his defense improved towards the end of the season, his shooting numbers waned.<ref name="2017evaluation" /> In general, his sophomore season was underwhelming, and with reduced minutes his game averages dropped to just 4.9 points and 2.2 rebounds per game on 35.5 field goal percentage.<ref name="2017evaluation" /> The Magic finished the season with 29–53 record, missing the [[2017 NBA playoffs|playoffs]].{{fact|date=March 2022}}

;2017–18 season
On 31 October 2017, Hezonja's fourth-year option was not picked up by the Magic.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=1 November 2017 |title=Won't Let Contract Situation Distract Him |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/mario-hezonja-wont-let-contract-situation-distract-him |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref>

After seeing very little action in the beginning of the 2017–18 season, he made first start of the season against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on 9 December and scored 7 points. On 13 December in a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], he scored a season-high 17 points and had nine rebounds, four assists and three blocks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Williams pours in 31 as Clippers dump Magic|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-orl-lac-writethru/williams-pours-in-31-as-clippers-dump-magic-idUSMTZEDCEXJF42L|access-date=18 December 2017|work=reuters.com|date=14 December 2017}}</ref> On 17 December, Hezonja scored a then-career-high 28 points and had six rebounds and two assists, while shooting 8 from 12 from the three-point line, in a 114–110 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite news |date=17 December 2017 |title=Hezonja scores career-high 28, Magic's late rally falls short against Pistons |work=foxsports.com |agency=AP |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/mario-hezonja-scores-career-high-28-magics-late-rally-falls-short-against-pistons |access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref>

=== New York Knicks (2018–2019) ===
On 6 July 2018, Hezonja signed a one-year, $6.5 million deal with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Widdoes |first=Charlie |date=6 July 2018 |title=New York Knicks Sign Mario Hezonja |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-mario-hezonja |access-date=9 April 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On 17 March 2019, he made a game-winning block against [[LeBron James]] in a 124–123 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Watch: Mario Hezonja Blocks LeBron James to Secure Knicks' Comeback Win Over Lakers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/03/17/lebron-james-mario-hezonja-game-winning-block-knicks-lakers-video |access-date=January 28, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=17 March 2019 }}</ref> Hezonja recorded 17 points, eight rebounds and two steals alongside the block.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks block LeBron at the finish, rally to beat Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071715 |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref> On 5 April, he recorded his first career [[triple-double]], logging 16 points, 16 rebounds and eleven assists in a 96–120 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Harden scores 26 in Rockets' 120-96 blowout win over Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071857 |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref> Two days later, Hezonja scored a career-high 30 points, alongside six rebounds, five assists and two steals, in a 113–110 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks rally in 4th, end long home losing streak to Wizards |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071877 |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2020)===
On 3 July 2019, Hezonja signed a two-year, $3.7 million deal with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=3 July 2019 |title=Trail Blazers Sign Forward Mario Hezonja |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-mario-hezonja |access-date=9 April 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 20 November 2020, Hezonja was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team trade involving [[Enes Kanter Freedom]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Grizzlies acquire draft rights to Desmond Bane and Mario Hezonja in three-team trade with Celtics and Trail Blazers |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-draft-rights-to-desmond-bane-and-mario-hezonja-in-three-team-trade-with-celtics-and-trail-blazers-201120 |website=nba.com |access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> On 11 December, the Grizzlies waived Hezonja.<ref name="CaverHezonja">{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Ahmad Caver Grizzlies Waive Mario Hezonja|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-ahmad-caver-201211|date=December 11, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 11, 2020}}</ref>
===Panathinaikos (2021)===
On 22 February 2021, [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] signed Hezonja for the remainder of 2020–21 season. There was an option on his contract for an additional year (until 30 June 2022), with a buy-out clause from [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] estimated around €400,000. Enes Kanter Freedom, Hezonja's Turkish teammate on the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], allegedly played a vital part in his transfer to the Greek powerhouse, having also expressed his sympathies towards both Panathinaikos and the country of Greece in the past.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hezonja In Green|url=https://www.paobc.gr/en/press-releases/102469_hezonja-green|date=February 22, 2021|website=paobc.gr|access-date=February 22, 2021}}</ref>

=== UNICS (2021–2022) ===
On 31 July 2021, Hezonja signed with the Russian team [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]], and of the [[EuroLeague]] until it was suspended due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mario Hezonja signs with UNICS Kazan|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1233984/unics-kazan-adds-mario-hezonja/|access-date=January 30, 2022|website=Eurohoops|date=31 July 2021 }}</ref> On 26 January 2022, he was named a [[VTB United League All-Star Game|VTB United League All-Star]], as part of the World Stars team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shved, Hezonja, McCollum and John Brown headline VTB All-Star Game lineups|url=https://basketnews.com/news-164629-shved-hezonja-mccollum-and-john-brown-headline-vtb-all-star-game-lineups.html|access-date=January 30, 2022|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

=== Real Madrid (2022–2026) ===
On 21 July 2022, Hezonja joined reigning Spanish champions [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hezonja joins Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/21/hezonja-joins-real-madrid|access-date=July 21, 2022|website=Realmadrid.com}}</ref> He won the EuroLeague in 2023 and was runner-up in 2024. On 2 July 2024, Hezonja signed a five-year contract extension with the Spanish powerhouse.

On 28 September 2024, Hezonja was sidelined for an unspecified amount of time after getting ill and losing weight as a result.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mario Hezonja sidelined after losing 7 kilos due to illness |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1720186/mario-hezonja-sidelined-after-losing-7-kilos-due-to-illness/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=28 September 2024}}</ref> On 2 October, he had resumed practices but was still questionable on returning to action.<ref>{{cite web |title=Madrid’s Hezonja recovers but is questionable for the Munich trip |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1721929/chus-mateo-talks-mario-hezonja-real-madrid-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=2 October 2024}}</ref>

On 1 June 2026, Hezonja was awarded the Spanish Liga MVP, having helped Madrid to the top of the standings after averaging 17.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 1.9 assists across 44 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hezonja receives the MVP and Best Five awards of the League|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/basket/first-team/latest-news/hezonja-recibe-sus-trofeos-de-la-liga-endesa-02-06-2026|access-date=July 15, 2026|website=realmadrid.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2026–present) ===
On July 26, 2026, Hezonja signed a one–year, $2.85 million contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], making his return to the NBA after a six-year absence.<ref name="NBA_2026_CavsSignHezonja">{{Cite web |date=2026-07-31 |title=Cavaliers Sign Mario Hezonja |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-mario-hezonja-260731 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]] |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260731182646/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-mario-hezonja-260731|archive-date=2026-07-31}}</ref><ref name="ESPN_Charania2026">{{Cite news |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2026-07-26 |title=Cavs, former lottery pick Mario Hezonja agree on 1-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49456228/cavs-former-lottery-pick-mario-hezonja-agree-1-year-deal |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260726181649/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49456228/cavs-former-lottery-pick-mario-hezonja-agree-1-year-deal |archive-date=2026-07-26 |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Hezonja was named Most Valuable Player of the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], after leading his team with a [[double-double]] in the final, 21 points, 10 rebounds and three steals.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.coid_FxtbjQqyId2WVafytY6os2.articleMode_on.html |title=Super Mario Leads Croatia to Gold|first=Dan|last=Casey|publisher=FIBA Europe.com |date=7 August 2011 }}</ref> Over the tournament, he averaged 20 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists. He was named to the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]] of the [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2012 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]].{{fact|date=March 2022}}

Hezonja was part of the senior [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]] that participated at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. He also represented Croatia at the [[EuroBasket 2015]],<ref>{{cite news|title=CROATIA UNVEIL AMBITIOUS EUROBASKET SQUAD|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=4 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913045910/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=13 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> where they were eliminated in the eighth finals by the [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CZECHS MAKE FIRST QUARTER-FINAL TRIP|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=.eurobasket2015.org|date=13 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914214822/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=14 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Over six tournament games, he averaged 6.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists on 41.2% shooting from the field.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mario Hezonja|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_2168.playerID_86032.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905090504/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_2168.playerID_86032.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=5 September 2015|website=eurobasket2015.org|publisher=FIBA Europe|access-date=13 September 2015}}</ref>

He represented Croatia at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], where they finished in 5th place.{{fact|date=March 2022}}
